model_response: After gold was found on Cherokee land in 1829 and Georgia pressed to take it, Congress passed the Indian Removal Act in 1830. By the end of that year, Jackson was telling Congress that removal was nearly finished and good for everyone, while the Cherokee - who had a written constitution, a newspaper and their own government - were asking the American people to stop it.
